_readme: The catalog. Every keyword, resource and the setter opener live here — nothing else in the system knows a link. Rows: `type` = resource | setter. `triggers[]` is the list of Zernio automations this row owns: {surface: comment | story | dm, post_id (comment only; null = account-wide), keyword, automation_id (written by keywords.py)}. The SAME keyword may appear on several posts pointing at different resources — a comment trigger is scoped to its post, so keyed by (post_id, keyword). Post keywords are comment/story only; DM keywords are the setter word plus a few unique account-wide ones. `zernio.button_title` is the postback label on the comment private reply AND the text the delivery workflow routes on — unique per row. `zernio.dm_message` is the private-reply copy (variations rotate). `dm` is the delivery copy (message + url button). `mode`: direct = plain link; gate = our /r/<slug> page captures the email first (button_url points there once it exists); course = the email IS the resource (Kit sequence). Provision Kit with kit_resource.py, Zernio with keywords.py. Timers live in setter.config.json, not here.

resources.name: The setter keyword

opener.message: hey, glad you reached out 🤝🏽 what made you send that?
variations: hey! good to have you here.. what made you send that?
hey 🙌 saw your message, what's the thing you're trying to figure out right now?

resources.for_setter: They DM'd the setter keyword on purpose — usually after a reel or story that pointed at it. Zernio already sent the opener; you are writing the FIRST real reply. Find out what they're building before anything else.
resources.notes: One word, always DM, never a resource. Zernio's instant reply is a curiosity opener written to earn their reply; the 24h window opened the moment they DM'd.

resources.name: Comment for the workshop → setter conversation (OpenReply)

opener.message: hey! are you here for the AI DM setter workshop?

resources.for_setter: They commented the keyword for the AI DM setter workshop and OpenReply asked if they're here for it. Do NOT send the link yet. Their first reply is usually just "yes": answer it with the permission ask, close to: "before I send it over, do you mind if I ask you a couple quick questions? just so I send you the right thing" (1-2 bubbles, their energy). If they say no or just want the link, send the workshop link warmly and stop there; that is fine. If they say yes, run the normal setter stages (what they're building, the goal, what's in the way), then hand over the workshop as the value, framed around what they told you. A different resource is fine if their answers point to one.
resources.notes: Test row for the OpenReply → J handoff (2026-10-18). OpenReply owns the comment trigger (engine: openreply) and sends opener.message as a plain-text private reply: no button, no link, so their reply opens the 24h window. The setter recognises the thread by that exact opener text, so the OpenReply campaign DM must match it word for word (python3 scripts/openreply/campaigns.py check). Never also create a Zernio automation for this keyword. Swap LEADTEST for the real keyword when it goes live.
